from.note_beginner: Go easy on nitrogen fertilizer; the soft, lush growth it pushes is what aphids swarm to.
Blast colonies off with a strong jet of water, hitting under the leaves and inside the head where they hide.
from.note_seasoned: Aim under the leaves and into the head; the waxy gray-green cabbage aphid is the hardest to dislodge and to wash out of a cut head.

from.note_beginner: Lady beetles and lacewings usually clean up aphids on their own if you do not spray them off.
For heavier clusters, coat the aphids directly under the leaves; repeat every few days.
